gen-gf-autour-one-gf-ubuntu-sans: Chunky, round and full of nerve. Ubuntu Sans backs it with tubular strokes like bent copper pipe and big lowercase eyes, which gives Autour One a body text that feels friendly rather than fussy.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-armata: Tall, blunt and a bit odd. Armata carries the sans-serif load with spacious gaps between characters, while Gugi swaps thin hairline joins for full-width stroke connections.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-liter: Upright, loud and slightly quirky. Gugi's open-cut terminals sit above Liter, whose stroke contrast is exactly none, so the headline gets attention and the text stays easy going.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-miriam-libre: Tall letters, open cuts, plenty of attitude. Gugi handles the loud, distinctive announcing, while Miriam Libre, a sans-serif with wire-weight strokes and cast-iron stature, does the quieter, friendlier talking.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Sharp, tall and unmistakably Gugi. Its curves match its stems exactly, so it earns its keep big and short, while Mochiy Pop P One lets a wide stretch of space sit between letters.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Noto Sans Bamum reads with big open counters and curved strokes that stop before they turn inward. Gugi, with its rope-fine strokes, is best loud and distinctive, while the body is best at keeping text modern and clean.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Tall, stroke-steady and slightly rebellious. Noto Sans Brahmi sets its mean line high and leaves every curve open-ended, so a long passage would read lightly, with Gugi's bold shapes left to the heading.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads softly, its ink strokes tapering out before they touch. A long passage in it would feel approachable and smooth, with hardly any step between capitals and lowercase.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Chunky, tall and a little cheeky. Gugi does bold best, with no swelling where curves meet stems, while Noto Sans Ugaritic does approachable best, its open mouths like a chalk arc left unjoined.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-stack-sans-text: Goldman comes in wide and commanding. Stack Sans Text follows with a marker-like constant line and big-bodied lowercase, so a longer passage would read smooth and unhurried beneath that bold display.
